claims.text: Decoder-only LLM predictions for cyberattack tactics suffer from low precision while achieving high recall.
Hallucinations in decoder-only LLMs during TTP analysis typically occur during the decoding phase.
Generic prompts tend to yield better predictions of cyberattack tactics than specifically tailored prompts.

evidence.description: The decoder-only results could suffer low ‘Precision’ while achieving high ‘Recall’
indicating the hallucinations typically occur during decoding phase.
Our findings further highlight a counter-intuitive observation that more generic prompts tend to yield better predictions of cyberattack tactics than those that are more specifically tailored.

methodologies.name: Comparison of SFT Encoder-Only vs RAG Decoder-Only LLMs
methodologies.description: Evaluates small-scale encoder-only LLMs using Supervised Fine-Tuning against large-scale decoder-only LLMs using Retrieval Augmented Generation for summarizing and comprehending attack procedures and tactics.

limitations.text: Interpretation of TTPs in the MITRE ATT&CK framework can be challenging due to presumed expertise and complex dependencies.
Decoder-only LLMs with RAG suffer from low precision and hallucinations during the decoding phase.
